question.text: The integral $\int_0^\pi \frac{8 x d x}{4 \cos ^2 x+\sin ^2 x}$ is equal to

solution.text:
$\begin{aligned}
& I=\int_0^\pi \frac{8 x d x}{4 \cos ^2 x+\sin ^2 x} \\ & I=\int_0^\pi \frac{8(\pi-x) d x}{4 \cos ^2 x+\sin ^2 x}
\end{aligned}$
$2 \mathrm{I}=8 \pi \int_0^\pi \frac{d x}{4 \cos ^2 x+\sin ^2 x}$
$2 \mathrm{I}=8 \pi \times 2 \int_0^{\pi / 2} \frac{\sec ^2 x}{4+\tan ^2 \mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=8 \pi \int_0^{\infty} \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{4+\mathrm{t}^2}=8 \pi \times \frac{1}{2}\left(\tan ^{-1} \frac{\mathrm{t}}{2}\right]_0^{\infty} \\ & =4 \pi \times \frac{\pi}{2}=2 \pi^2
\end{aligned}$
option (1)
